prompt: I've got a fresh Vite + React + TypeScript app (deps already installed: @tanstack/react-query, axios, zod, react-router). I need a 'tasks' feature: a page that lists tasks from GET /tasks and lets you create one with POST /tasks (fields: title, description). Please structure the code the way you'd structure a production app that's going to grow to many features — set up whatever folder structure and conventions you think are right, don't just dump it all in App.tsx.
assertions: Feature code lives in a dedicated feature module (src/features/tasks/...), not in flat top-level folders or App.tsx
One API file per endpoint under the feature's api/ folder, each exporting a typed fetcher function that uses a shared API client instance
The list query exports a queryOptions factory and a hook that accepts a queryConfig override parameter (configurable hook)
The create mutation validates input with an exported zod schema and its hook accepts a mutationConfig override parameter
The query key is defined in exactly one place; mutation invalidation reuses the factory's queryKey instead of retyping a string-literal key
No barrel index.ts re-export files in the feature module — feature code is imported directly from defining files (shared ui component barrels are acceptable, matching the reference app)
All new files and folders are kebab-case
ESLint import/no-restricted-paths boundary zones are configured, including a zone entry protecting the tasks feature
